hypotheses.justification: hB is used only as `hB.prod measurableSet_Ioc` to supply the measurability argument of `setIntegral_congr_ae` in two places (hleft and hright). In both places the integrands are equal at every point, not only on the set. In hleft, the proof's `hqmem` is never used; the step `buGaussian_timeShift_point_symm_apply σ q` holds for all q. In hright, `simp [F]` proves the equality pointwise. So the set-integral congruence can be replaced by `congr 1; funext q; ...` or `integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall ...)`, and that needs no measurability of the set. The change-of-variables step `MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_image_emb` with `τprod.measurableEmbedding` holds for arbitrary sets. `setIntegral_parabolic_to_product` has no measurability hypothesis (its implicit arguments are only Ω, I, F). `himage` is purely set-theoretic. The remaining steps are unchanged. The statement is therefore still true and provable for arbitrary B.
